messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Multiple OOMs during model warmup on cluster us-west-2a. Affected service: runtime-warmup. 90% error rate on warmup tasks over the last 3m. Fault signature: CUDA OOM + deserialize exceptions. Pager: oncall Alice Chen

Alice Chen: I'm on it, paging SRE. Any visible customer impact?

Raj Patel: looking at node telemetry now. GPUs showing repeated allocation failures, memory attribution spikes during artifact deserialization. Also seeing compile-timeouts for the model artifact (likely JIT).

Maya Lopez: I see the same on the infra dashboard — a subset of nodes (r-gpupool-8*) hit OOM then container restarted. Warmup concurrency is 4 by default; several warmup jobs started at once for a recent rollout.

Emma Rivera: Support report: two customers reported failed requests and increased latency in the last 10m. They saw 502/503 and a few partial streaming disconnects. Ticket numbers: SUP-8421, SUP-8422.

Alice Chen: Ok, immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle warmup concurrency to 1 for the pool, 2) temporarily disable model compile step (fallback to run without JIT), 3) route new warmup requests to fallback pool in another AZ. Can someone run the throttles?

Maya Lopez: I can flip concurrency. Pushing config now to r-gpupool-8* -> warmup.concurrency=1

infra-bot: config change applied to 12 hosts in r-gpupool-8* (gitops: warmup-concurrency-20260315).

Raj Patel: Disabling compile step on warmup worker via runtime flag `--no-jit-compile` for warmup only. Patching hotpath now.

Alice Chen: Before we do more, we need to capture a failing artifact. Raj, can you dump the warmup container logs and the first 256 bytes of the model artifact header? Suspecting corrupted header leads to allocator mis-estimate.

Raj Patel: Pasted log excerpt below:

```
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] warmup: starting artifact load /models/hf/llama-3b/v1/artifact.bin
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] warmup: deserialize header -> declared_tensor_count=123456789 (suspicious)
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] runtime: attempting allocate 180GB on GPU0
[2026-03-15T14:02:13Z] runtime: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation -> OOM
[2026-03-15T14:02:13Z] warmup: compile step timeout after 30s
[2026-03-15T14:02:14Z] container: exiting with code 137
```

Raj Patel: Header dump (first 128 bytes, base64): `SGVhZGVyQ29ycnVwdGlvbjogc29tZV9vZmZfZm9ybWF0IGRhdGEg...` — looks malformed, length fields are garbage.

Alice Chen: That aligns with deserialization error causing huge allocate. Good catch. We should stop warmup on any node that attempts to load that artifact. Maya, can you add an admission check to reject artifact headers with tensor_count > 10M? Temporary heuristic until we patch the artifact validator.

Maya Lopez: Pushing admission gate to warmup service: reject if declared_tensor_count > 10_000_000. Rolling to r-gpupool-8* with 50% rollout to avoid global disruption.

infra-bot: admission-gate rollout: 6/12 hosts updated.

Tom Briggs: Customer impact update: SUP-8421 is a paying enterprise on Dedicated — they saw ~18 failed requests in the window but reconnected after retry. They want ETA.

Emma Rivera: Let’s keep them updated in 15m windows. No data exfil or model response corruption observed. It's purely failure-to-serve.

Raj Patel: With concurrency reduced and compile disabled, new warmups are proceeding but some artifacts fail quickly due to header validation and are rejected. OOMs have dropped from 22/min to 0/min on the pool. Latency for serving unaffected for already-running models.

Alice Chen: Good. Next: identify source of malformed artifact. Who deployed the model variant recently?

Maya Lopez: Deploy log: artifact push 2026-03-15T13:58:01 by build-bot from pipeline `ml/llama-3b-quant`. The storage SHA is s3://redwood-models/llama-3b/v1/sha-abc123. We need to verify the artifact integrity.

Raj Patel: Running `sha256sum` on replica — mismatch on host r-gpupool-8-4. Possible partial upload.

Alice Chen: Isolation: mark artifact as suspect and prevent further warmups from pulling it. Add the artifact tag `quarantine:suspect` in model registry.

Maya Lopez: Registry updated: tag added. Also initiated background copy from a healthy replica and re-validated checksum. Fresh copy started to s3://recovery/..

Alice Chen: For immediate customer-facing help: enable automatic fallback to the quantized 8-bit variant (pre-validated) for requests referencing the problematic model id. How do we switch routing?

Raj Patel: We can add a routing rule in the control plane: if model.id == llama-3b:v1 and artifact.tag == suspect -> route to llama-3b:fp16-q8:v1. Applying now to hosted API only.

infra-bot: routing rule applied (control-plane change id: CP-20260315-001).

Tom Briggs: Notifying affected customers with mitigation steps and ETA for full restore.

Emma Rivera: Sent update to SUP-8421 and SUP-8422. Messaging: We detected corrupted model artifact that caused warmup OOMs; we've quarantined the artifact and implemented routing to a validated fallback variant. We're monitoring and will follow up when fully restored.

Alice Chen: Evidence so far: 1) malformed header led to huge allocation attempt, 2) compile-timeouts exacerbated resource retention, 3) concurrent warmups amplified impact. Mitigations taken: throttle concurrency, disable compile for warmups, admission-gate on header, quarantine artifact, route to fallback variant, and copy a healthy artifact replica.

Maya Lopez: Post-mitigation metrics: OOMs -> 0, container restarts reduced, warmup failure rate down from 90% -> 8% (mostly due to other old artifacts). Serving error rate for customers in affected pool returned to baseline.

Raj Patel: I'm going to collect heap dumps and full artifact for dev/repro. Plan to add stronger header validation in runtime and a prewarm checksum step. Also increasing compile timeout to 120s as a stopgap (30s -> 120s) to avoid mid-compile aborts causing weird partial states.

Alice Chen: Sounds good. I'll open the incident ticket and set SEV to P2 for now (customer impact limited; mitigation in place). Action items:
- Raj: postmortem PR with reproducible test and header check — due EOD + link to artifact sample
- Maya: ensure artifact registry has stricter upload validation and fails pipeline when checksum mismatches — due +24h
- Platform: add warmup concurrency as a knob in console + set default to 1 for new pools — due +72h
- Support: follow up with affected customers and link to incident ticket — ongoing

Tom Briggs: I'll handle customer comms and ask for any alpha customers impacted to accept credits if needed.

Alice Chen: Handoff: I'm going to eat dinner, handing oncall to Maya for the next 2 hours. If something regresses — page me and escalate.

Maya Lopez: Acknowledged, taking handoff. Will monitor the admission gate rollout and artifact copy.

infra-bot: Handoff recorded: from Alice Chen -> Maya Lopez at 2026-03-15T16:12:00Z.

Raj Patel: I've uploaded logs and the artifact sample to /incidents/3009876543/artifacts/ for triage.

Emma Rivera: Support will send a 1-hr status update at 16:30 UTC.

Alice Chen: Thanks team. Quick recap: corrupted model header triggered oversized GPU alloc -> OOM -> container restarts; mitigations applied (concurrency throttle, compile disable on warmup, header admission gate, artifact quarantine, routing fallback). No evidence of data loss. Monitoring until artifact restore and checksum verified.

Maya Lopez: Will keep thread updated. :thumbsup:

[end of thread]
